assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock combines laser cooling, precise atomic structure and spectroscopy to give fractional frequency uncertainties near 1e-18. This is a clear, original idea with large metrological consequences: a redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy, and tests of fundamental constants. It is atomic physics at its most disciplined, with atomic-structure calculations of polarizabilities and blackbody shifts at the core.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept (2001-2003) and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clocks. Ye's group brought the clocks to the highest accuracy and stability and developed many-body clock physics. The credit supports a clean two-laureate prize. Other contributors, including the Paris and Boulder groups, are not in the credited list, so the allocation is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Several independent groups worldwide reproduce and exceed the performance, and comparisons between clocks are routine. Recognition is timely, since the redefinition of the second is under discussion.
uncertainties: Whether Ye's role is better described as the leading realisation than as a co-invention.
Whether Nobel recognition should be held until the redefinition of the second is settled.
Whether the committee would treat this as covered by the 2005 and 2012 prizes on frequency combs and trapped-ion clocks.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned the quantum no-cloning and measurement principle into a practical protocol with provable security. It created a lasting field linking foundations and technology and is a natural complement to the 2022 prize on entanglement and Bell tests. Its originality and clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: BB84 (Bennett and Brassard, 1984) is the decisive invention. Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol was an independent and important contribution, but a prize built around BB84 can be fair with two laureates. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not on the credited list, which leaves a historical allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Mature in principle, with decades of experiments and commercial and satellite deployments. Practical security with real devices remains an active question, though this does not weaken the original discovery.
uncertainties: Whether Ekert should be included given the independent E91 route.
Wiesner's unpublished early conjugate-coding work and the question of his credit.
Whether deployment loopholes (device imperfections, side channels) bear on the lasting scientific impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect, together with the HgTe observation, opened a major field of topological band theory and spin-orbit physics. The concept is original and clear, and it has been influential well beyond its starting materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the Z2 classification and the graphene model. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe quantum well realisation, and Molenkamp's group observed it, but Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not among the credited names, so a theory plus experiment configuration cannot reflect the full chain. The 3D topological insulator route (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore and Balents; Hsieh and Hasan) is also outside this entry. Credit is therefore partial.
assessment.maturity: Mature and extensively confirmed by independent groups in multiple materials. Still, the allocation of credit in this field is contested, and the 2016 prize recognised topological phases in a related sense.
uncertainties: The missing HgTe theory proposers (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) in the credited list.
Overlap with the 2016 prize and with competing ideas for the three-dimensional case.
Whether graphene's spin-orbit gap is too small to count as a verified realisation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions defined a concrete architecture for quantum computation, and the high-fidelity ion-trap gates and entanglement experiments realised it. This is quantum optics and atomic physics in close contact with the technique I know best, and it has driven a large field.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal, and Blatt's group built many of the decisive experimental demonstrations, such as entangled states of many ions and quantum simulations. Wineland and Haroche were already recognised in 2012 for controlling single quantum systems, which narrows what is left to credit. Other experimental groups (Monroe, Wineland, Innsbruck, NIST) share the experimental work and are not all listed.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature. Trapped-ion processors are commercial and scaling continues. The question is whether the key discovery is already covered by the 2012 prize and whether any single feat of quantum computation is yet decisive.
uncertainties: How much of the experimental credit lies with groups outside the list.
Overlap with the 2012 prize.
Whether the quantum-computing outcome is settled enough to judge long-term impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire materials field. The prediction came before the experiment, and the results were striking and clear. The impact on correlated-electron physics is large.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 prediction. Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery. This gives a natural theory plus experiment configuration. Cao and others in the experimental group, and other theorists of related continuum models (for example Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto), are not credited, so the allocation of credit is not fully clean.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently in several laboratories, but the pairing mechanism and many correlated phases are still being debated. Recognition would be reasonably timely but somewhat early, as the field is young.
uncertainties: The nature of the superconducting pairing.
Credit for early continuum-model work by other theorists.
Whether sample-dependence and twist-angle disorder still limit the clean picture.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry with laser-cooled atoms underlies precision measurements of gravity, rotation and the fine-structure constant, and it supports tests of the equivalence principle. It builds directly on laser cooling and the control of atomic wave functions, and its original ideas have had a lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Bordé contributed the theory of atom interferometers with light pulses. Pritchard realised early atom interferometers and the Mach-Zehnder style devices, and Kasevich developed the light-pulse gravimeters and gradiometers. Chu, Ketterle, Cornell and Wieman were recognised earlier in related areas, and other groups (Chu, Bongs, Rasel) also contributed, so the credit is spread across more people than three names can cover.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with commercial gravimeters and quantum-sensing use. The main discovery is established; larger-scale fundamental tests remain in progress.
uncertainties: Dispersion of credit among several equally important groups.
Overlap with the 1997 and 2001 prizes.
Whether the discovery is a single clear result or a family of techniques.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics brought cavity-QED ideas, which I know well from atomic physics, into superconducting circuits and enabled strong coupling, dispersive readout and the transmon-based processors. Its originality is clear and its impact on quantum technology is large.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin, Huang, Schoelkopf and Wallraff produced the 2004 proposal and the first strong-coupling experiments. Four names are credited, so three must be chosen, and any choice leaves out a decisive contributor. Koch, Schreier and the transmon work also play a role. The allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely reproduced. However, the 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, so a closely related award so soon would be a question of timing.
uncertainties: Which three of four credited people carry the decisive contribution.
Proximity to the 2025 prize.
Role of the transmon design as a separate part of the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters, and the superfluid to Mott insulator transition in particular was a clean and important demonstration. Quantum gas microscopes then allowed single-site resolved many-body physics. The idea of quantum simulation is influential and the work is of high quality.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch, Zoller and others proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation, and Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott insulator experiment and the microscope work. Five credited names exceed the prize limit, and Jaksch and others who also made the proposal are absent, so the configuration is difficult. Ketterle, Cornell and Wieman were already recognised in 2001 for condensation.
assessment.maturity: Mature in its basic results, which are reproduced in many laboratories. The goal of solving open problems in condensed matter with quantum simulators is still only partly realised.
uncertainties: Whether a three-person prize can represent proposals plus experiments.
Overlap of Zoller with other candidates and with the 2001 prize area.
How far quantum simulators have already delivered new physics.
